records.statement: Bidang Euklides adalah ruang metrik dengan sedikitnya dua titik.
Melalui setiap dua titik berbeda terdapat tepat satu garis.
Setiap sudut menentukan ukuran sudut berarah dalam (-π, π].
Untuk setiap sinar awal dan setiap ukuran yang diizinkan terdapat tepat satu sinar akhir.
Fungsi ukuran sudut kontinu pada domain yang dinyatakan dalam sumber.
Kekongruenan segitiga setara dengan dua kesamaan sisi dan kesamaan sudut berarah apit hingga tanda ±.
Perbesaran positif pada dua sinar memperbesar sisi ketiga dan mempertahankan dua ukuran sudut terkait.

records.description: The source emits a label whose text duplicates the immediately following index key; the stable label is preserved unchanged for compatibility.
The stable exercise label spells obtuse as obtuce; the identifier is preserved unchanged for reference compatibility.
The stable exercise label spells obtuse as obtuce; the identifier is preserved unchanged for reference compatibility.
The source switches from the introduced motion X maps to X' to an undefined symbol f; the Indonesian prose says 'the isometric transformation' to preserve the evident referent.
The Indonesian construction explicitly draws and extends the perpendicular segment from P, avoiding the nonsensical reading that an already infinite line is extended.
The Indonesian proof explicitly states that m and n are respectively the perpendicular bisectors of AB and BC, preserving the intended pairing.
The Indonesian exercise attaches 'through the given point' to the tangent lines rather than to the given circle, preserving the intended construction task.
The full Indonesian section title is retained in the reader while a shorter optional title is used in the running head to prevent collision with the page number.
The chapter titled Similar triangles retains the legacy source label chap:parallel for reference compatibility.

The exercise declares O, A, B, C, A', B', and C' distinct while allowing every k greater than zero; at k=1 its ray-and-distance hypotheses force A'=A, B'=B, and C'=C. The source statement is preserved unchanged.
The commented-out footpoint exercise and hint retain inherited triange misspellings and English prose as inactive source surfaces; they remain excluded from the active exercise-hint closure.

The Indonesian proof explicitly says that angle BAX is added to the left-hand side and angle CAD to the right-hand side, clarifying which corresponding sides produce angle BAD without changing the argument.
The chapter titled Parallel lines retains the legacy source label chap:angle-sum for reference compatibility.
The active similar-triangles-with-a-parallel-line exercise retains the inherited smililar spelling in its source label for reference compatibility.
The active Apollonius-locus exercise retains the inherited apolonnius spelling in its source label for reference compatibility.
The active Apollonius construction exercise retains the inherited apolonnius spelling in its source label for reference compatibility.

The commented-out pi-over-four isosceles exercise, its English hint with an inherited plus-or-minus sign conclusion, and inactive figures pic-92 and pic-334 remain commented source surfaces and are excluded from active exercise-hint and figure closure.

In the only-if proof, the Indonesian reader says that the reflected line ell-prime and m both pass through Q, correcting the authority's P: reflection across midpoint O sends P to Q, and the theorem assumes m passes through Q.
The Indonesian hint uses D not equal to B, rather than the authority's D not equal to C, to rule out the positive oriented-angle sign in the rhombus argument.

The Indonesian hint begins its SSS equivalence with AB=AD, the adjacent-side condition characterizing a rhombus, instead of the authority's automatically true opposite-side equality AB=CD for a parallelogram.

The Indonesian construction exercise states A not equal to B, M outside the pair {A,B}, and AM not equal to BM, excluding coincident foci, zero or undefined focus ratios, and the k=1 perpendicular-bisector case that is not a circle.
The Indonesian index keys follow the definition's nondegenerate quadrangle term rather than inheriting the authority's degenerate-quadrangle keys.

The inherited forced page break and its unresolved editorial marker are omitted, while the visible Sifat transversal heading receives a one-em leading gap without changing its table-of-contents or running text; content, mathematics, and source order are unchanged, and the reflow has passed visual admission.

Reader-facing Indonesian syntax, terminology, punctuation, and referent order are normalized throughout without source-order or meaning change; one same-side sentence moves the math token m before ell, producing an explicitly allowlisted math-sequence delete-and-insert pair.

The Indonesian reader associates the bisectors of angles ABC, BCA, and CAB with vertices B, C, and A respectively, correcting the authority's incompatible A, B, C correspondence while preserving the three angles and their order.

The Indonesian incenter proof says 'the same proposition' when it invokes prop:angle-bisect-dist a second time, matching the source environment's Proposition kind instead of the authority prose's 'same lemma'.
The authority alternates 'external bisector' and 'exterior bisector' for the same object; the Indonesian reader and backend consistently use garis bagi luar.
The midpoint-quadrangle exercise retains the inherited midle spelling in its active source label for reference compatibility.
The external-angle-bisector exercise retains the inherited disect spelling in its active source label for reference compatibility.

The source explicitly uses altitude for both a perpendicular line and the corresponding distance; the Indonesian reader distinguishes garis tinggi from tinggi, and the backend represents the two senses with linked concept IDs.
The Euler-line hint begins by directing the learner to read about homothety without citing a self-contained source; the dependency is preserved and indexed for later solutions/mastery closure.

The bisector-equals-median hint retains its reference to the distinct source label ex:abs-bisect=median; admission must keep the cross-chapter target resolvable rather than normalizing the labels together.

Excenter is introduced and defined only in the authored hint for the obtuse-triangle analogue; the backend gives it a concept ID so semantic and accessible readers do not omit the hint-only definition.

The Indonesian figure replaces the visible authority labels 'bisector' and 'external bisector' with 'garis bagi' and 'garis bagi luar'; geometry, source figure number, and drawing topology are unchanged.
